description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of proactive and reactive emotion regulation during expressive suppression and cognitive reappraisal of negative emotional images.

spans.text: Using event-related fMRI, we investigated neural correlates while participants were anticipating reappraisal or suppression (proactive, cue phase), as well as while they were applying these ERS (reactive, target phase), all within the context of negative, high-arousing emotions.

description.value: Participants prepared to suppress and then suppress the outward display of their feelings elicited by each negative, high-arousing picture, without holding the face still beforehand; they were instructed that people in their environment should not be able to see what they were feeling.

description.value: Participants prepared to down-regulate their emotions and then cognitively reappraised each negative, high-arousing picture by generating an alternative, less negative interpretation of the depicted situation, changing the emotions, actions, and outcomes of the individuals depicted.

description.value: Participants made no preparatory-control response, simply looked at each negative, high-arousing picture, felt their natural feelings, and did not change anything.
